key_insight: A mass-lumped finite element scheme preserves phase-field values in [-1, 1] and dissipates the original discrete energy without time-step restrictions, even with degenerate mobility.
engineering_relevance: The method supports robust phase-separation simulations by maintaining physical bounds and energy decay when mobility vanishes at pure phases.
method: Use continuous, piecewise-linear, mass-lumped finite elements on non-obtuse meshes.
Apply convex splitting to the double-well potential in time.
Establish bound preservation and energy dissipation using operator monotonicity and split-potential convexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments confirming the theoretical properties and robustness in degenerate-mobility phase-separation dynamics, but provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on a non-obtuse mesh condition; unconditional stability does not imply time-step-independent accuracy.
paper_title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation
